newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin hopes for compromise on Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin hopes for compromise on Belarus.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin called on Tuesday for compromise and common sense in neighbouring Belarus and said he was worried about the rise in tension there, the Kremlin said.

Spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin had discussed Belarus at a 90-minute meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin. "The president and the prime minister expressed alarm about rising tension in Belarus society and the hope that common sense and the art of political compromise will replace the ambitions and confrontations among politicians," he said.
It was Yeltsin's first official meeting since his open heart surgery two weeks ago. The Russian president is recovering from the operation at the Central Clinical Hospital on the outskirts of Moscow.
Russian officials have been keeping a low profile on the situation in Belarus, where President Alexander Lukashenko has called a referendum asking voters to give him additional powers.

The Minsk parliament opposes the proposals and has drafted its own questions for the referendum, due to take place on Sunday. Deputies have been occupying parliament around the clock since Friday to protest at Lukashenko's ideas.
